what_happened: Job 20261112-112705-q134 (code job: hold kill-switch-stopped jobs as resumable, not failed) failed in planning, before any code was written. The planner reached its fixed 600-second deadline without finishing a plan. The event lists no critic findings, no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered, and no partial plan or reason was kept.
cause: The planner stage has a fixed 600s wall-clock deadline. It keeps no partial plan, gives no progress signal, and has no resume or retry path. Nothing sizes the request against that deadline before planning starts, and nothing records what the planner was doing when time ran out. A deadline stop therefore discards all planning spend and leaves no diagnosis. The same request wording (kill-switch stopped vs failed) already timed out in case 20261114-112627-efkg, and this job looks like a re-ask of that request. Nothing carried that failure into this attempt, such as narrowing the scope or raising the deadline.
other_causes: The request touches job lifecycle states (stopped, failed, resumable), status output and retry, so it probably spans several surfaces and needs a large plan.
A re-ask of a deadline-failed job goes through the same planner with the same limits and no extra information.
open_hypotheses: The request may be too large for one 600s planning run. The fields cannot show how big the plan was.
The planner may have been slow for other reasons, such as exploring the code or an environment slowdown. No progress record exists to tell.
This job may be a retry or re-ask of 20261030-113229-kgrg. The fields do not say.
prevention: Make the planner survive its deadline. It should write a partial plan or progress notes as it works, and on a deadline stop it should record the stage it reached and the reason. Before planning, a size check should flag requests spanning several surfaces and split them into one-change jobs. A retry after a planner deadline should start from the saved partial plan, or from a narrower request, and not repeat the same full run. Gate counts give no basis for relax or remove: every gate shows 0 disagreements.
proposed_request: Make planning-stage deadline stops recoverable. When the planner reaches its time deadline, Athena must (1) record the last stage reached and the reason in the job record, (2) keep any partial plan written so far, and (3) hold the job as resumable instead of failed. A retry must resume from the kept partial plan. Acceptance: a test with a fake planner that exceeds the deadline shows the partial plan and the reason are stored, and a retry starts from the stored plan. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
